items.title: Tutor Perini (TPC) Q2 Earnings and Revenues Top Estimates
items.summary: Tutor Perini (TPC) delivered earnings and revenue surprises of +27.94% and +4.80%, respectively, for the quarter ended June 2026. Do the numbers hold clues to what lies ahead for the stock?

items.title: Tutor Perini (NYSE:TPC) Reports Strong Q2 CY2026
items.summary: General contracting company Tutor Perini (NYSE:TPC) reported Q2 CY2026 results exceeding the market’s revenue expectations, with sales up 19.2% year on year to $1.64 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $1.74 per share was 37.6% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

items.title: Dow Makes More New Highs Despite AI Drag: Stock Market Today
items.summary: Stocks were mostly higher again as Iran and Oman negotiated a shipping agreement for the Strait of Hormuz, but AI capex is still a big issue for investors.

items.title: $58 billion In Payouts, A Lagging Stock: The T Trade-Off
items.summary: The telecom giant showered shareholders with cash while the stock itself went nowhere, forcing a hard question about what all that money actually bought.

items.title: These Stocks Are Making Moves Today, Thanks to SpaceX
items.summary: SpaceX has designs to leverage its dominant position in the space business into a dominant position in AI and communications.  SpaceX stock, for starters, was down about 12% at $110.  Nvidia shares were up 3.1% partly because SpaceX is using their chips for its Starmind AI computing satellites.

items.title: Lumen Posts Narrower-Than-Expected Q2 Loss, Revenues Drop Y/Y
items.summary: LUMN's Q2 loss came in narrower than expected as strategic revenues have risen 14.1% and free cash flow has turned positive despite a 9.3% revenue decline.

items.title: Telecom shares decline as SpaceX outlines plans for mobile network expansion
items.summary: Shares of major U. S. wireless providers moved lower after SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) revealed plans to develop a fully integrated mobile service, raising concerns that Starlink could eventually become a direct competitor to Verizon (NYSE:VZ), AT&T (NYSE:T) and T-Mobile (NASDAQ:TMUS).
